pages.text: A capacitor bank dumps a current I through a coil of N turns and length L: the field is B = μ₀NI/L. The coil's resistance turns the current into heat, ΔT ∝ NI²t over the pulse t; the magnetic pressure B²/2μ₀ pushes the coil outward. Every storey of the room is another stack of plates and its cooling: more copper to soak up the heat.
$(thing)Set$(): Turns, Peak current, Pulse length.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Capacitor charge: the current varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): The coil is melting; The magnetic pressure is tearing the coil apart.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Shorter pulses recharge faster.
